searchText: Hmm, let me go back and look at this. I was only considering the (value), but you're right a more accurate count would be (address, value) for accounts and (address, slot, value) for storage items. Isn't that number like 100x smaller than *current state*. Right now I think I'm slightly overestimating and I'm getting ~31GiB when considering every (address, value) and every (address, slot, value) I shouldn't be surprised that the hashes are so heavy, but I'm still surprised! Currently writing something to include intermediate nodes in that count From a geth node that fast synced: ``` | Key-Value store | Contract codes | 1.65 GiB | 342754 | | Key-Value store | Trie nodes | 90.95 GiB | 734913979 | | Key-Value store | Trie preimages | 1.48 GiB | 22404303 | | Key-Value store | Account snapshot | 5.28 GiB | 112674883 | | Key-Value store | Storage snapshot | 28.08 GiB | 395129891 | ``` I'm not 100% sure how to interpret each of those numbers but my guess is that the snapshot storage doesn't de-duplicate so for the leaf data we can expect something around 5.28+28.08GB But those 90.95GB of trie nodes are.... large We'll also have to duplicate contract code.... What is a storage snapshot in this context? Geth's flat database layout What is trie nodes then? And the storage is the contract storage part (I'm infering) geth uses both flat and naive database layouts concurrently IIRC. I don't know exactly why... Oh, trie nodes are non-leafs, account/storage are leaves? If so, I didn't previously realize how much more expensive trie maintenance was compared to actual data storage. I guess I shouldn't be surprised given that most storage is less than 256-bits, and it will require >256-bits of branch space in most cases. Not definitive but I think "Trie nodes" is the full trie, both intermediate and leaf nodes. and "XXX snapshot" are just the leaf data. I don't know what preimages are referring to preimage will be the original key and then it's actually stored in the trie under the hash to ensure an even distribution.
